heroText: Mbabane is Eswatini's administrative capital, a small hillside town in the Highveld overshadowed in size by nearby Manzini and the Ezulwini Valley resorts. First-time visitors should hike Sibebe Rock, one of the world's largest granite monoliths, browse the market and shops along Gwamile Street, and day-trip into the Ezulwini Valley for craft markets and hot springs. King Mswati III International Airport, over an hour away, is the country's main gateway.

areas.name: Mbabane CBD
areas.text: The Mbabane CBD centres on Gwamile Street and Swazi Plaza, walkable in under an hour and convenient for shops, banks and the market.

areas.name: Ezulwini Valley
areas.text: The Ezulwini Valley, just southeast of Mbabane, is Eswatini's main resort area with hotels, hot springs and craft markets close to Lobamba.

areas.name: Mbabane West
areas.text: Mbabane West is a residential suburb on the edge of town, a quieter option for longer stays within easy reach of the CBD.

airports.name: King Mswati III International Airport (SHO)
airports.search: King Mswati III International Airport, Eswatini
airports.text: King Mswati III International Airport lies over an hour's drive from Mbabane; confirm transfer arrangements in advance since public transport options are limited.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between King Mswati III International Airport (SHO) and central Mbabane before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in the Mbabane CBD for walking access to Gwamile Street and the market, or choose the Ezulwini Valley for resorts, hot springs and easier access to craft markets. Mbabane West suits quieter, longer stays close to the centre.
hotelIntro: Mbabane hotel choice often comes down to pace: the CBD keeps shops and banks within walking distance, the Ezulwini Valley offers Eswatini's main resort hotels and hot springs, and Mbabane West provides a calmer residential alternative.
rentalCars: A rental car is useful for reaching the Ezulwini Valley, Sibebe Rock and other sights spread beyond the compact CBD.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay in the Mbabane CBD for walking access to shops and the market, or the Ezulwini Valley for resort hotels and hot springs.

travelTips.title: Airport transfer
travelTips.text: Budget over an hour for the drive from King Mswati III International Airport, and arrange transport in advance for late arrivals.

travelTips.title: Sibebe Rock hike
travelTips.text: Set aside a morning to hike Sibebe Rock, wearing sturdy shoes and carrying water, since there's little shade on the exposed granite dome.

travelTips.title: Craft shopping
travelTips.text: Combine a visit to the Ezulwini Valley with stops at Ngwenya Glass and Swazi Candles, both well-known local craft workshops.

highlights.title: Mbabane Market
highlights.text: Mbabane Market gives Mbabane a concrete street-life stop, with food, everyday shopping and local movement that helps visitors read the city.

highlights.title: Sibebe Rock
highlights.text: Sibebe Rock gives Mbabane a greener or more scenic stop, useful when the route needs views, shade, walking space or a slower hour.

highlights.title: Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary
highlights.text: Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary is a named stop in Mbabane worth keeping on the route when it fits the day's transport, timing and neighborhood plan.

highlights.text: Mantenga Cultural Village gives Mbabane a strong culture stop for museums, exhibitions or local collections, and works best as an indoor anchor in the day's route.

highlights.title: King Sobhuza II Memorial Park
highlights.text: King Sobhuza II Memorial Park adds outdoor time to a Mbabane stay, with open space, views or waterfront breathing room between denser city sights.

nearbyIdeas.name: Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary
nearbyIdeas.label: Wildlife
nearbyIdeas.text: Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary near the Ezulwini Valley offers walking and biking trails among zebra, antelope and warthog, a relaxed half-day trip from Mbabane.

nearbyIdeas.name: Ngwenya Glass
nearbyIdeas.label: Craft
nearbyIdeas.text: Ngwenya Glass, near the border with South Africa, is a well-known recycled-glass workshop and a popular stop for handmade souvenirs.

history.text: Mbabane was founded in 1887 by Mickey Wells, on the spot where the Transvaal-to-Mozambique route crossed the Mbabane river.
The town grew after the nation's administrative centre was moved from Bremersdorp (now called Manzini) in January 1902.

history.label: 1930s
history.text: By the 1930s, Mbabane had electricity, running water, telephone connection and a hospital.

history.label: Growth
history.text: It derives its name from a chief, Mbabane Kunene, who lived in the area when some British settlers arrived.

history.label: Civic role
history.text: During this time, Mbabane consisted of a few shops, churches and schools founded by white settlers.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The black Swazi Africans were not allowed to live in the town and had to reside in nearby rural districts.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Prior to WW2, most Swazis lived in rural districts and worked outside Eswatini, so there was little growth in the town.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: In the years following independence, governmental buildings such as the British Consulate were built in Mbabane.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Growth has occurred with the tourism industry in Eswatini, of which Mbabane has become the centre.
